### Declared residual lookaheads

- **BEA CAINC1 / CAGDP2**: BEA revises. The 2020 value read here is the revision present in the 2026-07-20 file, not the estimate published at the time. Irreducible without archived vintages; W1.3 audit residual.
- **StatCan 23-10-0256 transborder O&D**: Table discontinued after reference year 2018. A planner at 2022-01 would have wanted 2021 and could only have had 2018. This is the frozen model's own anchor limitation, reproduced faithfully at vintage.
- **Census CBSA delineation**: Published 2023-07, after this cutoff. Only list1_2023.xlsx is cached; historical delineations are not available offline, so counties are rolled up to 2023 metro boundaries anyway. W1.3 audit vector L4, irreducible under the no-network rule.
- **carrier operating-to-brand map**: carrier_families.csv and carrier_codes.csv carry no effective dates, and segment_brands() resolves from a fixed DB1B year. Air Wisconsin flew for American to 2023 and United after; Mesa's American agreement ended 2023. W1.3 audit vector L3, not fixed during Milestone A.

## 7. Defects the replay exposed. Measured, not fixed.

Milestone A records defects and Phase 6 fixes them under a change report. None of the following was changed to produce these results.

### D1. The corridor-growth term collapses transborder demand at a COVID vintage

Anchored transborder demand is `anchor x growth`, where growth is a raw ratio of T-100 corridor traffic in the latest complete year to the anchor year, with no COVID handling of any kind.

| cutoff | growth year | YYC growth | YYZ growth | YYC transfer | YYZ transfer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 202201 | 2019 | 1.057 | 1.014 | 2.258 | 1.406 |
| 202301 | 2021 | 0.196 | 0.166 | 1.785 | 1.104 |
| 202401 | 2022 | 0.739 | 0.665 | 1.485 | 0.980 |

At the 2023-01 cutoff the latest complete T-100 year is 2021, so growth is **0.196** at YYC and **0.166** at YYZ. Every anchored WestJet market is scaled to roughly a fifth of its 2018 level:

| study | cutoff | method | n | median demand | median margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| porter_yyz | 202401 | anchor_x_growth | 66 | 21,003 | -301% |
| porter_yyz | 202401 | unanchored_capped_at_ceiling | 22 | 2,661 | -1,750% |
| westjet_yyc | 202201 | anchor_x_growth | 37 | 13,156 | -174% |
| westjet_yyc | 202201 | unanchored_capped_at_ceiling | 51 | 4,227 | -687% |
| westjet_yyc | 202301 | anchor_x_growth | 30 | 2,023 | -3,829% |
| westjet_yyc | 202301 | unanchored_capped_at_ceiling | 50 | 783 | -8,120% |
| westjet_yyc | 202401 | anchor_x_growth | 26 | 6,467 | -785% |
| westjet_yyc | 202401 | gravity_x_transfer | 1 | 2,624 | -2,583% |
| westjet_yyc | 202401 | unanchored_capped_at_ceiling | 49 | 2,956 | -1,600% |

**Consequence for reading these results.** The 2023-01 WestJet cell is dominated by this artifact: median margin around -3,800% and every market PASS. Its five positives are therefore scored by a model that believed the market had shrunk 80%. The 2024-01 cell is affected less severely (growth 0.739) and 2022-01 barely at all (growth 1.057).

**This is a point-in-time behaviour, not a replay bug.** A planner in January 2023 genuinely saw depressed 2021 traffic. What no planner would have done is treat it as a permanent level shift with no recovery expectation, and the frozen model has no mechanism to do otherwise. Production avoids the problem only because it happens to read 2024.

The protocol admits 2021 as input data while excluding it as a decision vintage, with the rationale recorded in `config/replay_protocol.yaml` **before** the replay ran: a planner at 2023-01 did in fact hold 2021 data. That was a design choice made in advance, so it stands as primary. Excluding 2021 as data too would move the 2023-01 growth year back to 2019; that is a permitted labelled sensitivity and is not run here.

### D2. Right-sizing has no discriminating power

The model chose the minimum of its frequency option list on 18 of 18 paired launches, and on 461 of 463 decision rows across the whole replay. Observed openings on those same launches span 0.9 to 20.0 weekly.

A constant cannot correlate with anything. WestJet's median ratio of 1.00 is not evidence of calibration; it means WestJet's recent openings happen to be thin. Alaska and Porter both under-size significantly, with bootstrap intervals on the ratio excluding 1.0.

This refines the Stage 0 prior rather than confirming it. Stage 0 compared all historical spells against the current all-3x screen and inferred a uniform downward bias. Paired properly, the bias is study-specific: absent at WestJet, roughly a factor of two at Alaska and Porter.

### D3. Family 2 cohorts differ from the Stage 0 counts, by definition

The protocol defines outcomes as register spells for the study brand, hub and US destinations, **without** the candidate-set distance and population gate. Stage 0 applied that gate. The Family 2 counts here are therefore not directly comparable to Stage 0's, and neither is wrong. Recorded so the difference does not read as drift.
